overall_assessment:
One medium regression-harness finding remains: NUM-ADH-CP36D-01. The current production adapter throws the correct class, the new production mapper is narrow and safe, and the browser double imports that actual production constructor. The finding concerns the lost assertion that connects those independently tested boundaries, not an observed current production wrong-class failure. No new production P1/P2 defect or security regression was established in this bounded static review. This is an architecture/adherence/security supplement, not acceptance of final TQA, the running all command, runtime recovery, external validation or the whole delivery.

Scope and provenance: I read the bounded dispatch/package, approved Contract Boundary and D-01..D-10 baseline, module consistency/security context, nine allowed public files and exact-path diffs against API f134bd11449a553e6f57e66cdc8fc71032151060 and Web d33c82c26760c671d98cab6f3e7bfe5676122c69. All nine current hashes matched cp36d-source-before.sha256 again before writing this result. Comparison with cp36c-source-after.sha256 confirms four unchanged API loci and five changed loci: ChannelsService, Meta unit spec, flow PG spec, browser fixture and Web telas test. I directly inspected the untracked convergence helper and necessary public caller/credential/lease/session/DI/error/runner code. Prior source-bound cp36c judgments are preserved only at unchanged loci. No tests, builds, runtime/provider/network actions, Git mutations, delegation, private dotenv, .local-files or operator-data access occurred. Only this named result is written.

Security assessment: the broader TODO remains high risk because it crosses OAuth, credentials, mutable grants, webhooks and tenant boundaries. For this source supplement I examined foreign-BU access, stale/cancelled attempts, numeric versus null epoch, wrong identity/current owner, receipt-less open, lost lease, forged continuation URLs and error-detail exposure. The existing caller fences remain effective by source inspection; the helper depends on those trusted callers rather than providing an independent authorization entry point. The Meta adapter uses the fixed Graph host/version, encoded resource path, URLSearchParams for the opaque cursor, explicit scoped authorization and redirect:error (meta.client.ts:106-124,178-195). Provider next URLs are continuation signals only and are never followed. Missing/empty/non-string/oversized cursor with a next signal is inconclusive; cycles and continuation after the second page also stop. No fresh threat-intelligence retrieval or attack simulation was performed in this read-only/no-network supplement. Prior accepted attack simulations are preserved only for unchanged loci, and no waiver is created.

Fixture and test efficacy: browser-server.cjs:3 imports MetaIndisponivelError from the exact same dist Meta module as META_CLIENT, and its new inconclusive branches instantiate it at :94 and :97. There is no duplicate constructor or generic Error in those branches. TQA-CP36C-02's source parity defect is therefore corrected; its current-platform acceptance is still pending. The new BFF negative reaches the real Nest/session/CSRF/Prisma application and the fake verifier's two-page loop by spying only on numerosDaWaba (flow:110-121; helpers.ts:72-84). It asserts two exact WABA/token/cursor calls, 503/catalog, retained channel observations/current attempt/generation/epoch/receipt, unchanged attempt version, identity, credential metadata and BU, released lease and no success audit (flow:123-139). These are meaningful DB/transport assertions. They do not execute real Graph HTTP; only the real adapter HTTP-stub unit tests establish its debug-one plus pages-two request budget. The newly changed code-only adapter rejection assertions leave the constructor-composition hole in NUM-ADH-CP36D-01; existing class assertions for other adapter operations do not exercise these pagination branches.

Both Web changes are legitimate preconditions, not a product Persons change or a retry-only workaround. contaNova creates this account's Numero de QA (telas.spec.ts:8-19); both existing cases select it using the real Numero control, register a wait for the real POST /api/bff/usuarios before clicking, and require 201 before checking the original Ana/sector and Bia/fallback-link outcomes (338-391). Global page-error/console checks still apply, and no 400 is ignored (59-75). Usuarios.tsx:24-38,55-62,95-98 confirms the asynchronous BU/form dependency being made explicit. The exact cause of cp36c's old Ana 400 was not captured; neither these edits nor this review claims to have diagnosed or repaired the product loading race.

Performance, elegance and structure: the mapper adds no query/network work, broad catch, global filter, status-200 fallback or generic provider framework. The shared convergence helper keeps the repeated-state policy in one small owned function rather than diverging per caller. Its extra read is scoped by attempt primary key only when promotion misses. Meta verification is bounded to one grant request and at most two phone pages, each with a ten-second AbortSignal under a 45-second lease, with lease/fence checks after successful I/O and again at commit. There is no provider fan-out in listing or DB transaction across HTTP. These source properties are acceptable and show no new material performance/elegance/structural regression. Old PCV envelopes are not new throughput/SLO measurements. Operational fit is mixed because the required integrated current evidence, test repair disposition and external recovery remain open.

P1/P2 and Rule-Spirit: no current production P1/P2 defect was established, but the medium test finding should be completed before claiming robust protection of the typed public error contract. The changed tests retain their original business outcomes; no skip/only, sleep/retry acceptance, ambient row selection, BFF mock, broad catch, false success, SQL repair or new product flag appears in the scoped diff. No raw RED was reconstructed and no historical failed command was relabeled. The remaining constructor assertion gap is an efficacy weakness, not evidence of deliberate rule evasion.

Evidence limits and verification debt: the named cp36d RED log really contains MetaIndisponivelError, observed status 500/catalogCode null, 141 unit passes and 287 PG passes/one expected BFF failure (red-full.log:239-249,432-456). It proves the pre-mapper BFF boundary using typed provider injection. The final fake two-page-loop strengthening was added afterward and was not separately rerun RED; it must not be represented as a second pre-fix paging reproduction. The inspected final-all tail still showed PG progress, not a completed all result. At dispatch the API leaf and browser were not green for these bytes; this report accepts no terminal all/TQA/freshness evidence by inference. cp36c all remains failed, and its malformed-dispatch TQA raw remains advisory rather than an accepted gate. Existing mixed/test-after debt, the unavailable original cp36 raw stdout, and old RED status-only limits remain explicit. The recorded dependency audit of eight affected packages (one critical, six high, one moderate), private OWNER/synthetic-cohort restriction and security-backlog deadline before untrusted users are unchanged; this review performed no new dependency scan or advisory refresh. The postcommit/prepublication crash gap, lack of outbox/autoreplay/ordering guarantee and absence of continuous-health proof remain. Corrected local runtime recovery, fresh human unofficial IN/OUT02, and real official OAuth/selected TEST resource/IN/OUT/recovery are mandatory and unwaived. TODO remains active Pending with the D-06 runtime Exception; no runtime/publication/whole-delivery authorization follows from this supplement.
recommended_path: Recommend a small serialized test completion for NUM-ADH-CP36D-01 before accepting the affected typed-error regression harness: retain both constructor and catalog-code assertions for each same real-adapter rejection, without issuing duplicate operations or weakening request counts. Current product mapper, DB/lease fences, actual browser constructor and the two existing invite preconditions can stand. Preserve this frozen run and its raw result; wait for live readers and the current all to terminate before any source edit, then refresh the impacted canonical evidence/freeze and obtain the required fresh TQA/final adjudication through root. Do not reopen unchanged architecture, expand into Persons product behavior, add a global filter, or relax identity/epoch/CAS predicates. D-05/D-07 source correction is present, while integrated validation and the D-06 runtime Exception remain open. Root must keep final all, TQA, runtime, official external proof and whole-delivery acceptance separate; none is granted here.

findings.title: Real-adapter pagination negatives no longer prove the error constructor required by the mapper
findings.rationale: api-app/src/integrations/meta/meta.client.spec.ts:169,181,186,191 now assert only rejects.toMatchObject({ code: 'META_INDISPONIVEL' }); the previous constructor checks in these affected negative cases have been replaced. The new application boundary deliberately recognizes instanceof MetaIndisponivelError only (channels.service.ts:291). Its BFF/PG negative executes the separately implemented typed fake loop (flow:110-121; helpers.ts:72-84), while the browser uses another separately implemented typed fake (browser-server.cjs:3,94,97). Counterexample by source inspection, not an executed mutation: replacing a real pagination throw with Object.assign(new Error('safe inconclusive'), { code: 'META_INDISPONIVEL' }) preserves the newly asserted unit code and fetch counts. The independent typed-fake BFF/browser cases also remain satisfied, yet a real verify request bypasses instanceof and again returns generic 500. Class assertions elsewhere in this spec cover different operations and do not close that branch-specific hole. Why now: cp36d introduces constructor identity as the production transport-mapping predicate while replacing the exact adapter class assertions that could protect it. Current production throws are the correct class; this is a concrete regression-harness efficacy gap at the same error boundary just repaired, not a claim that current production already emits the wrong type. Blast radius is the persisted official-number unavailable/inconclusive response contract; no owner/DB security regression was found.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): for each affected invalid-grant/budget/cycle/oversized-cursor operation, retain its single rejected promise or captured rejection and assert both toBeInstanceOf(MetaIndisponivelError) and code META_INDISPONIVEL on that same result. Keep current scoped arguments and exact fetch-count assertions; do not call the operation a second time merely to inspect another property. This is a small test-only change with low implementation/runtime risk, one-spec blast radius, no added network/query cost and low maintenance. It restores the simple composition contract without altering the sound narrow production catch. Root should serialize it after the live review/run and refresh the affected evidence rather than attributing later bytes to this freeze. B: add a faithful real MetaHttpClient HTTP-stub -> service/BFF contract test for the same budget failure. That can prove the composition directly, but needs more wiring and maintenance than restoring the lost assertion. C: keep code-only units and rely on static inspection plus typed provider fakes. No immediate production edit is needed, but this leaves the concrete generic-500 regression undetected by the new harness; not recommended for closure of this repaired boundary. Broadening production mapping to any object with a matching code would change the approved error boundary and is not an appropriate test repair. Root owns the authoritative finding disposition, current validation and acceptance.
